newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air aircraft talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air aircraft talks continue.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said talks for a pending aircraft acquisition have intensified, but no decision has been made.
Delta said it continues to negotiate with both Boeing Co and Airbus Industrie for a "major" aircraft purchase, but declined to comment on the extent of the possible order.
Airbus said Delta's decision is imminent, but declined further comment. Boeing could not be reached for comment.

Delta plans to replace its aging fleet of L-1011 aircraft with either the Airbus Industrie 330, the Boeing Co 777, or the Boeing 767-400. As of the end of fiscal year ended June 30, Delta had 38 domestic L-1011s and 17 international L-1011s.
Delta previously said it also may purchase other aircraft, but did not provide additional details. Analysts said Delta could announce a order for about 100 aircraft.
The value of the pending order would be in the billions of dollars, but the exact cost depends on the mix of planes purchased.

The Boeing 777 has a retail cost $128 to $171 million. Boeing said it has not set a price for the new 767-400 model, but the closest comparison is the 767-300-ER model, priced at $96-$107 million. Airbus officials were not immediately available to comment on pricing.

Delta, the nation's third largest airline, recently reorganized its tranAtlantic, European and domestic routes. Replacing the aging fleet and improving customer service are the next hurdles Delta must face in its effort to increase marketshare and attractive more lucrative business class travelers, analysts said.
